verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents provisioning on-demand GPU instances from the web search page and through the CLI and REST API. Its CLI walkthrough covers the full flow: search for a GPU, rent it, wait for boot, connect, and run code over SSH or Jupyter. The docs also claim instances spin up in seconds, and a runtime probe confirmed the CLI exposes create and destroy instance commands. Missing for 10: hands-on verification of the end-to-end create-to-running time (the probe only ran search, not instance creation), and independent corroboration of boot speed; one community report also describes extra hoops compared with AWS/GCP.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision an on-demand GPU instance from the console or API and be running code on it within minutes

citations.quote: The search page is the main portal for finding good machines and creating instances on them.
search for a GPU, rent it, wait for it to boot, connect to it, copy data, and clean up
The Vast.ai REST API gives you programmatic control over the entire platform.
Spin up GPU instances in seconds at competitive prices.
Despite their large size you'll find they generally start quickly because they have been cached on many of the host machines.
`vastai --help` prints the full command surface including search offers, create instance, and destroy instance.
